summary: create the tasks that close the known code-level rule violations and deliver the missing authoring, progress and contract-quality surfaces
owner_direction:
Owner direction 2026-09-19 (third batch: create the missing work). Create new task contracts, with their phase README rows and todo/config.yaml entries, for the deliverables below. Do not modify any existing task contract, its dependency fields or its status; do not activate anything; do not delete a file; do not change behaviour of any existing gate. Every task you create must be deliverable from the repository alone, must add its acceptance criteria to the contract, and must not weaken any existing rule.

(1) A task that makes the implementation satisfy ADR-006's declared dependency direction, depending on T006. Its scope is exactly the violations that exist today and are recorded in docs/implement/DOCUMENTATION_INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md: the upward import in src/robinhood_lp/strategy/baselines.py lines 102 and 106, which ADR-006 lines 41-42 remedy by moving a genuinely shared type into a lower contracts/domain module rather than by relaxing the rule; the concrete-module imports in src/robinhood_lp/replay/replayer.py line 83 and src/robinhood_lp/replay/ticks.py line 87, which contradict ADR-006 line 31's requirement that reconstruction and features consume injected read ports rather than concrete storage modules; and src/robinhood_lp/qualification/hook_pack.py, whose own docstring forbids the config import it performs, so either the import or the docstring is wrong and the contract must say which is to be made true. Its acceptance must require that the corresponding entries in T006's exception list are removed rather than renewed, and that the layer check passes without them. Do not create layers for the five packages ADR-006 does not classify: the Owner has deferred that to a separate ADR, and T006 keeps those as dated exceptions.

(2) A task that delivers the strategy authoring guide under docs/implement/, so that an author who has only this repository can write a strategy the event-driven backtest engine will actually run: the callback shape the engine consults and when it is consulted, the field semantics and units of what it receives and returns, the fill and information-frontier assumptions, the prohibitions the layer carries, and a self-check an author can run. It must cite STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md section 7 and the task contracts as the normative sources rather than restating them as its own authority, and it must be written against the interface the specification now states, including which task owns the adapter between the engine callback and the strategy components.

(3) A task that delivers the on-demand global progress view over todo/config.yaml: a command that renders, in plain language, what each phase and task is for, where it stands, what is approved and not superseded, what is blocked or has changes requested, and what is ready next. It must be generated on demand and never committed as a file, must not record a HEAD SHA, a test count or any other fact that the next commit falsifies, and must be reachable without reading the raw configuration. It must not live under tools/workflow/, which no role may change. Its acceptance must include a test proving it renders from the committed configuration and a test proving the check can fail.

(4) A task that delivers the machine check that every task contract's Acceptance criteria are testable and that a quantitative rule stated in Deliverables is also required by Acceptance, since two already-confirmed economic rules reached the contracts through Deliverables alone. Reuse T006's exception mechanism with reason, owner and expiry, and include the test that proves the check can fail.

(5) The glossary: decide its home from the repository's own rules. If it must be normative it belongs under docs/spec/, which no developer task can write, so record that decision and the reason instead of creating a task that cannot deliver it.

Nothing outside the new contracts, their phase README rows, the new task entries in todo/config.yaml and the two revisions may change.
